correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and finite abelian H of cardinality q>=2, pointwise period Möbius inversion and subgroup character orthogonality give the exact coefficient formula. The largest eligible power q^d cannot cancel the sum of distinct smaller powers, proving support C_m and rank q^(n-m). All nonzero coefficients are divisible by q^m; strict union bound Σ_{p|rad(n)}q^(-m(p-1))<1 produces a frequency with exactly the minimal term, so the positive singular-value minimum is q^m. The trivial frequency attains the upper bound P_q(n), giving sharp inverse norm and condition number. Dual annihilator identifies the exact stabilizer U_m. Independent direct integer Walsh and exact cyclotomic/Klein tensor scripts replayed from actual new paths and checked all frequencies over specified finite ranges. No finite computation is used to infer the all-length result.

Known necklace Möbius inversion underlies the proof but alone does not give the noncancellation or optimal spectral endpoint. The nearest primary texts treat necklace indexing, perfect necklaces, or 2-adic span of an individual sequence. Folklore equivalence and an abstract-only historical source remain stated residual risks.

value.rationale: The full-period-word set is a central necklace/cyclic-word object, while its Fourier zero locus and translation stabilizer on the alphabet-product group are natural previously unquantified recovery invariants. The theorem gives an all-length, all-finite-abelian-alphabet classification, detects exactly the extra hidden period n/rad(n) symmetry, and supplies an optimal inverse norm and sharp condition number; its value is structural rather than a routine small numerical increment. Nonabelian alphabets, orbit representatives, and weighted words are explicitly out of scope.
